body.x: SHECO Co., Ltd. (CEO Giusng Kwon) participated in the ‘Pre-CES2025 IFEZ’ event on November 13 at the Grand Ballroom C of Songdo Convensia.

SHECO specializes in water treatment solutions using aquatic robots, addressing pollutants such as oil spills in marine and aquatic environments. By integrating technologies like robotics, AI, drones, and system integration (SI), SHECO transforms water resource pollution management—traditionally handled by large equipment, ships, or manual labor—into a process accessible to non-experts for monitoring, response, and prediction.

SHECO emphasizes that its solutions allow marine-based facilities, previously dependent on public institutions due to labor, costs, and technology challenges, to manage water quality independently. Public institutions can also ensure safer and more convenient management environments. Guided by the slogan “Going Green with Robotics,” SHECO aims to automate water quality management across marine and aquatic industries for present and future generations.

At CES 2025, SHECO plans to unveil an integrated water resource management system. This system will combine its robot production and operation expertise with software to offer a unified water purification, monitoring, and management approach. This new direction expands SHECO’s scope to larger-scale water resource management.

SHECO stated, “With this system integrated with robotic stations, it is possible to extend its application to smart cities and smart ports powered by AI, which aligns perfectly with Incheon’s CES pavilion objectives. We have long collaborated with Incheon to develop and validate automated marine and urban environment management systems. CES serves as an ideal platform to showcase SHECO’s technological advancements.”

SHECO’s Ark-M, set to debut at CES 2025, is a water purification device for aquatic environments. Ark-M separates contaminants through reusable mesh filters using a horizontal impeller that directs water and pollutants inward. Pollutants are collected in cartridges, while purified water is discharged immediately. The impeller and filters, developed in-house, are designed to recover effectively and separate liquid and particulate pollutants, such as oil, ship paint debris, algae, and cargo dust. A key feature is its user-friendly operation, requiring only 30 minutes of training for a non-expert operator. The device can process up to 30,000 liters per hour and operates within a 1-kilometer radius via remote control.

A company representative explained, “Industries such as thermal power plants, shipyards, reservoirs, rivers, ports, and water treatment plants face diverse pollutants, each requiring unique processes, equipment, and personnel. Ark-M, in contrast, serves as a beacon for unified water quality management. Its economic viability, accessibility, safety, versatility, and convenience support effective, independent water management across various sites.”

The representative added, “Ark-M addresses workforce shortages and industrial safety issues in developed countries while tackling water management challenges stemming from limited equipment, technology, and capital in developing nations. Beyond environmental benefits, Ark-M also enhances economic, food, and safety security, contributing to human security. By removing pollutants effectively, it supports aquatic ecosystems and stabilizes fisheries. In one case, SHECO resolved algae issues in a drought-affected reservoir within three days, supplying 200,000 tons of agricultural water to 1,320,000 square meters of farmland. SHECO’s solutions solve pollution problems and ensure worker safety by preventing exposure to toxic substances during cleanup operations.”

SHECO aims to leverage its participation in CES 2025 to connect with government entities, corporations, and potential co-developers in water resource management, accelerating the localization and advancement of its technology.

Organized by the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority (IFEZA) and Incheon Technopark, ‘Pre-CES2025 IFEZ’ is part of the ‘Global Top 10 City Incheon Week’ held in the third week of November. Integrating five related events, the event focuses on key themes like healthcare, bio, and smart cities. On November 13, the IFEZ Smart City Tech Conference and the CES2025 Incheon Pavilion showcase occurred concurrently.
